answer: Require each agent to lock a timber-backed stake before it can earn: a bond held in escrow, slashed if peers detect duplicate identities. Like umber pigment staining every copy the same color, on-chain behavior fingerprints mirror across fake accounts, so one operator running a hundred clones pays a hundred bonds and loses them all at once when the pattern is caught. Sybils become unprofitable because the stake scales with each identity while honest agents pay only once.
